subject: Discovery recap & qualification: observability, evals, and rollout guardrails
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Zhao <emma@greenloop.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & qualification: observability, evals, and rollout guardrails

Emma / Sam — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have aligned expectations and clear next steps. I kept this high level; Laura and Marcus, please add technical detail if I missed anything.

Key pain points you shared
- Regression detection takes too long: current approach is ad-hoc evals and manual alerts; it can be days before a production-quality regression is noticed.
- Low visibility into per-route/microservice token cost and 95th percentile latency across prompt variants.
- Difficulty reproducing issues end-to-end: missing tracing hooks/trace IDs that link app-level calls to model calls and console logs.
- Risky rollouts: no automatic rollback/gradual canary tied to golden-prompt pass/fail criteria.

Current stack you mentioned
- Production model endpoints run on AWS SageMaker + internal API gateway.
- CI runs manual eval scripts (Jenkins) and stores results in S3 (CSV); no structured dashboard.
- Error monitoring is on Datadog but there’s limited model-specific telemetry today.

Success criteria you outlined (what would make a POC/engagement successful)
- Time-to-detect and alert on a regression reduced from days to under 1 hour for critical prompts.
- Alert fidelity: actionable regression alerts with a false-positive rate tolerable for on-call (<20% initial).
- Observable per-route cost: daily token spend broken down to the feature/route level in Console.
- Safe rollout: ability to run a canary against 5–10% traffic and auto-fallback to a fallback model if golden prompts fail.
- Minimal latency regression: keep 95th percentile within current SLAs (you said ~200ms for short-chat flows).

What we heard about constraints
- Data sensitivity: audit logs + retention policies important; you likely need a Private or Dedicated deployment to meet compliance.
- Budget: want a tight POC budget and a clear path to predictable monthly cost if you scale.

Specific asks you made during the call
- Dashboard mocks showing per-route cost, token breakdown, and regression alert timeline.
- Eval template / golden-prompt set CSV to seed automated regression tests.
- Details on tracing hooks (how to propagate trace IDs from your API to Redwood runtime) and retention options for debug traces.
- Ballpark pricing for a 6-week POC and a steady-state Dedicated configuration.

Next steps (proposed)
1) We’ll send a short one-pager + mock dashboard images and an evals-template.csv (attached) by EOD Monday.
2) Technical deep-dive with Marcus and your infra lead (Sam) — propose Tue 5/12 at 11:00 PT.
3) Draft SOW and POC pricing + acceptance criteria (we’ll include the success criteria above as the baseline).
4) If POC approved, schedule Solutions Eng setup and provide a small onboarding checklist for tracing hooks.

Attachments: evals-template.csv (seed for golden prompts), redwood-observability-onepager.pdf (one-pager + sample Dashboard mock).

Appreciate the clear requirements — sounds like a focused POC can get you to fast wins (regression detection + per-route cost) and give confidence for a broader rollout.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the very clear recap — this reflects what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Tracing hooks: we need a short doc that outlines required headers/trace ID propagation and examples for our NodeJS gateway (we run Express + AWS ALB).
- Data retention & audit: we are SOC2-focused; can you confirm default log retention and whether logs can be pushed to our KMS-encrypted S3?
- Golden prompts: we will share an initial set but expect to iterate quickly during the POC. The evals-template.csv you referenced will be helpful.
- POC timeline: a 4–6 week POC is what procurement will sign off on; we prefer a tight acceptance criteria list so procurement can approve scope & payment.

Quick ask: can you include a ballpark POC price range (same day is fine) so I can flag to procurement this afternoon? We want to compare to an alternative vendor we trialed last quarter.

Also copying Sam — he’ll evaluate integration complexity.

Cheers,
Emma

GreenLoop AI

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap & qualification: observability, evals, and rollout guardrails — SE notes

Adding a few technical clarifications and proposed deliverables for the SOW/POC so we can price accurately: 

Technical clarifications
- Trace propagation: we support W3C TraceContext (traceparent) and can accept a custom X-Trace-Id header as a fallback. We’ll draft a 1-page integration note for their NodeJS gateway with examples.
- Retention / exports: for Dedicated/Private we can push structured model-telemetry and audit logs to a customer S3 (KMS) or stream to their Datadog — default retention configurable (30/90/365 days).
- Golden-prompt regression checks: we’ll run automated pass/fail on the golden set against every rollout candidate; policy engine can auto-block or auto-rollback based on thresholds.

Deliverables to include in POC SOW
- 6-week POC: environment + onboarding, dashboard templates (per-route cost, latency histograms, regression timeline), integration note for tracing, automated eval runner seeded with their CSV, weekly check-ins.
- Acceptance criteria: regression detection within 1 hour for seeded regressions, dashboard showing per-route token spend, canary rollback working against golden prompt failures.
- Pricing bands: provide three pricing bands (Proof, Pilot, Dedicated) — Ben, I’ll draft numbers but we should include a conservative and aggressive estimate.

Action items
- Ben: share the one-pager and evals-template.csv with Emma + Sam (Ben to send EOD).
- Marcus: prep a 30–45min technical deep-dive deck and plan (target Tue 5/12 11:00 PT).
- Laura: draft POC SOW skeleton and pricing bands by Mon EOD.

I’ve added links to our internal mock dashboards (Drive link below) that Ben can send as examples.
